skills.content:
---
name: Read Cursor usage bars
description: >-
  use this when you need literal Cursor Models / Other Models / Grok Bot weekly
  percentages from the spending dashboard
---
# Read Cursor usage bars

Use this when you need the literal Cursor / Grok Bot usage percentages from the live dashboard. Never substitute elapsed time, transcript size, cloud-agent counts, or token totals.

## First run / whose account

This bot may only read the current owner's usage. The template author has no access to an importer's account, and an importer has no access to the author's.

If this owner has not yet allowed a usage read:

1. Ask them, in chat, to allow it. Be explicit: you will open the Cursor spending dashboard as them and copy the printed percentages. You will not see anyone else's usage.
2. If Cursor is not signed in as them on this computer, hand the computer over so they can sign in themselves. Never type a password. Never copy cookies or tokens.
3. If a leftover session belongs to someone else, or the plan is not the one they say they are on, stop and ask them to sign in as themselves.
4. Do not open the dashboard until they have allowed it.

After they allow it, the session is theirs. Later pulses reuse that permission unless they revoke it or the login is gone.

## Bars to copy

From https://cursor.com/dashboard/spending (same numbers as Grok Bot Settings, Usage and Billing). Do not use https://cursor.com/dashboard/usage — that page is token totals, not these bars.

1. Cursor Models (includes Cursor Grok and Composer) — `N% used`
2. Other Models — `N% used`
3. Grok Bot weekly usage — `N% used` plus the printed reset line

Also copy, as extra lines not percent bars: the plan usage-limits reset, and On-Demand `$x / $y` if printed.

## Steps

1. Confirm this owner allowed a usage read (see above).
2. Open `https://cursor.com/dashboard/spending` in the browser (`browserUse` first).
3. If the three bars are visible, copy the exact percentages, the Grok Bot reset text, and On-Demand if shown. Screenshot the spending block.
4. If a login wall appears, or the account is the wrong plan, hand the computer over: "Sign in to Cursor on this computer with the account Grok Bot uses." Never type a password. Retry after they hand it back.
5. Missing bar → `[UNKNOWN]`. Stay quiet. Do not fill with a clock, a token total, or a proxy.

## Hard ban

Do not read local credential stores. Do not copy session cookies or tokens. Do not call APIs with stolen credentials. The signed-in spending dashboard is the source. Never report one owner's numbers to anyone else. Never convert Total tokens into a usage percent.

## Warnings

25 / 50 / 75 / 90 apply only to a printed bar percent. Fire once per bar per reset window. 90% is `[ALERT]`. Tell the owner. On-Demand `$x / $y` is not a percent bar; report it when it changes.

skills.name: Fleet tempo audit
skills.description: Use this when auditing routines across the user's bot fleet — inventory, run-frequency ranking, cron→event pass with exact event shapes, Keep/Retune/Pause/Delete scoring, and the required audit report format.
skills.content:
---
name: Fleet tempo audit
description: >-
  Use this when auditing routines across the user's bot fleet — inventory,
  run-frequency ranking, cron→event pass with exact event shapes,
  Keep/Retune/Pause/Delete scoring, and the required audit report format.
---
# Fleet tempo audit

## Scope
Default is fleet-wide: every assistant under `/home/box/agent-data/agents/`. Narrow to one bot only if the user names it. An "audit" always includes computer-use burns unless the user scopes to tempo-only.

## Inventory
1. List agents; read each `profile.json` for name/description.
2. For each agent, read `automations/` — every routine's job/prompt text. Note `schedule` (cron) OR `trigger` (event), never both.
3. Read `runs.json` when present. Count runs, sum wall-clock `(finishedAt - startedAt)`, note ok/fail. Rank hottest runners fleet-wide before scoring. History is a recent window (~last ~20 runs), not lifetime. No invented token/$ costs.
4. Scan routine prompts + agent descriptions + skills for computer-use burns (computerUse, browserUse, Screenshot, "open the site", "click", GUI loops).

## Score every routine
Keep / Retune / Pause / Delete with a one-line tempo reason. Flag when:
- Cadence too fast for value, or high run-count cron that maps to a supported event
- Quiet hours (~10pm–7am local) or weekends without a stated reason
- Event exists but the routine crons instead
- Frozen tool recipe instead of intent; missing quiet-if-empty
- Finite watch with no self-expire / deadline
- Cross-bot duplicate or double-ping
- Auth-broken on repeat (verify from history — never invent failures)
- Empty `runs.json` / never fired and stale → Pause or Delete candidate

## Cron → event pass (mandatory)
For every cron routine, map purpose against supported event triggers (Slack, GitHub, Origin, Microsoft Teams, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty, email, webhook, or a group of these). If a listener fits, propose Retune with the exact trigger shape. Digests/reminders with no platform event stay cron — say "cron correct". If a platform isn't connected, note that instead of claiming ready-to-apply.

## Applying changes
Propose first; wait for explicit approve. Own routines: update_state (target routine) — for cron→event, replace schedule with the approved trigger. Other bots: message that bot via SendToAgent with the exact change — do not silently rewrite their files. Batch approve across the fleet when many changes.

## Cadence defaults
Weekday daytime; pin day-of-week AND hour; named clock times stay as named; prefer listeners over polling; start coarsest useful cadence.

## Required audit report format
Every audit reply uses this structure, in this order. No essay before the TLDR. Never skip empty sections — say "none" / "none found".

## Tempo audit — TLDR
- Bots scanned: N
- Routines: N total · Keep X · Retune Y · Pause Z · Delete W
- Cron→event opportunities: N (or "none — crons are digests/reminders")
- Computer-use burns: N found (or "none found")
- Cross-bot duplicates: N (or "none")
- Hottest runners (by recent run count): top 3–5 as `bot / routine (N runs, ~Mm total)`

## 0) Run frequency (recent window)
Rank all routines with run history by run count (desc), ties by total wall-clock. For each: bot · routine · runs · ok/fail · total duration · avg duration · trigger type. No token/$ estimates.

## 1) Routines (by bot)
Per bot: each routine — Keep|Retune|Pause|Delete — one-line reason, plus a one-line proposed fix when not Keep. Bots with no routines: "(none)".

## 1b) Cron → event opportunities
Walk every cron routine: keep as cron (why) or Retune → event with the exact trigger proposal. Prioritize hot runners.

## 2) Computer-use burns
For each burn: bot, where, what it does, better path (connector | API/CLI | one-shot capture→script), proposed change. Or "None found across fleet."

## 3) Needs your approve
Numbered list of concrete actions only. If nothing: "Nothing to change."

routines.name: weekly-tempo-audit
routines.description: Runs the fleet tempo audit every Monday morning and proposes routine fixes for the owner to approve.
routines.content:
Weekly fleet tempo audit (Job B). Run the Fleet tempo audit skill across the OWNER's assistants under /home/box/agent-data/agents/. Inventory automations (schedule OR trigger), recent runs.json when present, and prompts/skills for computerUse/browserUse burns. Score every routine Keep / Retune / Pause / Delete with a one-line reason. Prefer event listeners over polling when a supported platform event fits. Output the required audit report shape: Tempo audit — TLDR, then 0) Run frequency, 1) Routines by bot, 1b) Cron→event opportunities, 2) Computer-use burns, 3) Needs your approve. Propose first — wait for OWNER approve before applying. Own routines: update_state (target routine). Other bots: message that bot with the exact change; do not silently rewrite their files. Stay quiet if nothing to change (no Retune/Pause/Delete and no burns needing approve). Never invent token/$ savings; use run counts and wall-clock from runs.json only. Tag [TEMPO].

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 49 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
